content.text:
The drawing shows a central CH carbon bonded to three groups: a morpholine nitrogen, a 2,4-dimethoxyphenyl ring, and a benzodioxole ring that carries an OH.

**Morpholine.** The ring contains O at the top and N at the bottom. N is attached to the central CH, so the group is N1CCOCC1.

**2,4-Dimethoxyphenyl.** The ring carbon attached to CH is C1. Going around the ring, the OMe at the bottom is on the adjacent carbon (C2). The H3CO at the upper left is on the carbon para to C1 (C4), so the pattern is 2,4-dimethoxy. As SMILES: c1(C...)c(OC)cc(OC)cc1.

**Benzodioxole with OH.** The ring carbon attached to CH sits next to a ring-fusion carbon, and its other neighbour bears the OH. Labelling the ring atoms:
- a1 is attached to CH.
- a2 is the aromatic CH between a1 and the fusion carbon at the top right.
- a3 is the top-right fusion carbon, bonded to O.
- a4 is the bottom-right fusion carbon, bonded to O.
- a5 is the aromatic CH at the bottom.
- a6 bears OH and is bonded to a1.

The OCH2O bridge links a3 and a4. As SMILES: c1(C...)cc2OCOc2cc1O.

**Assembled SMILES.** The CH carbon has no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is assigned:

C(N1CCOCC1)(c1ccc(OC)cc1OC)c1cc2OCOc2cc1O

Checking the dimethoxyphenyl ring in this string: c1ccc(OC)cc1OC starts at C1 (attached to CH), then C6, C5, C4 (OMe), C3, and C2 (OMe), which closes back to C1. The OMe groups are therefore at C4 and C2, as drawn.

SMILES: COc1ccc(C(N2CCOCC2)c2cc3OCOc3cc2O)c(OC)c1
